A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAC algorithm and LSBM recovery problem by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 Section 4 and Appendix G report original simulations comparing IAC with PLMLE on four synthetic SBM scenarios, including means, standard deviations, and boxplots from 100 experiment instances.

after.justification: v2 Appendix F retains these original simulation results, including Table 2 and four boxplots. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The spectral initialization changes from summing label adjacency matrices into one square matrix to horizontally concatenating the trimmed label-specific matrices. Algorithms 1–2 consequently preserve separate label information during initialization; the likelihood-based refinement phase remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four simple SBM scenarios: balanced symmetric, imbalanced, sparse symmetric, and sparse asymmetric. All use L=1. The newly discussed signed, censored, and multiplex models introduce no additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Both versions compare IAC against the computationally lighter PLMLE implementation, Algorithm 3 of Gao et al. (2017). v2's added discussion of full PLMLE attributes its performance to prior work and does not add an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The four scenarios retain their node counts, cluster counts and sizes, edge-probability parameters, and misclassified-node metric. Moving experiments to Appendix F introduces no reported protocol change; the computing environment is newly disclosed rather than revised.

E4.justification: The same benchmark comparisons and boxplots are retained, with no added ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error analysis. Model misspecification and adversarial noise appear only as future research directions in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations from 100 experiment instances and boxplots displaying outliers. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 contain identical statistics for all eight method–scenario combinations, and all four plotted result displays are unchanged. For example, Model 4 retains mean errors of 45.5600 for IAC and 54.7400 for PLMLE.

T1.justification: Assumption (A2) changes from squaring summed label differences to summing squared labelwise differences, admitting separation that aggregation can conceal; Appendix E.6 revises the corresponding derivation. Proposition 3.6, renumbered 4.6, drops the term counting nodes outside H from its premise, and the expectation proof revises its conditioning event. v1 Appendix C's reproduced lower-bound proof is removed, while Theorem 1.1 remains attributed to Yun and Proutiere (2016).

C1.justification: The central claims of instance-optimal recovery in expectation and with high probability, parameter-free operation, and near-linear complexity remain. Their claimed applicability broadens through the revised separation assumption. The stronger emphasis on necessary and sufficient conditions largely restates the existing matching-bound claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the mechanism discussion through asymmetric decision boundaries and nonlinear information geometry, including a conjecture that Euclidean spectral clustering alone cannot generally attain optimal rates. Sections 2.2–2.3 also explicitly distinguish the fixed-cluster, sparse setting from broader prior guarantees and identify multiplex models as an extension beyond the present framework.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix F.1 newly specifies macOS Sonoma, MATLAB, an Apple M3 Max processor, and 128 GB memory. Section 3.1 also explains exploiting sparse edge traversal during refinement. These additions improve implementation documentation without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 expands the comparison to Xu et al. (2020) on homogeneous labeled models, recent spectral-recovery work, and signed and multiplex networks. It develops new distinctions concerning heterogeneity, parameter dependence, computational cost, and guarantees. The spectral-noise lemma is now explicitly attributed to Le et al. (2017), with the retained proof positioned as an alternative.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds separate notation and main-results subsections, separates theoretical guarantees from the algorithm section, adds a technical-challenges discussion, and moves numerical experiments into Appendix F. The appendix contents page is removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to two columns, and the algorithms become column-width displays with numbered lines. The results table changes from model-wise column groups to stacked model–algorithm rows and moves to the appendix. The four existing plots are resized and repositioned without changing their displayed results.

improvement.justification: v2 improves research positioning and reproducibility documentation and introduces a construction intended to support broader labelwise separation. However, v1 Algorithm 2 powers a square matrix, whereas v2 Algorithm 2, line 7, still takes a matrix power after defining an n-by-nL concatenation, which is undefined as written for L>1. The unchanged L=1 experiments cannot resolve this inconsistency. The benefits therefore coexist with an unresolved defect in the central algorithm specification, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
